rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "Three agents using the file": "the file" (line 7, 8, 9) resolves to chunk 0 line 3's named `backlog-refinement-rules.md`. chunk 2 "The file is steady; the agent moves": line 13 "all three agents" and line 14 "Slack thread, issue event, daily schedule; Claude Code on the web, GitHub Actions, a scheduled agent" resolve to chunk 1's three named shapes and their mechanisms (lines 7-9). No forward-pointing or never-named referents found. Harm this rule prevents (a reader stranded mid-deck) is absent.
No callback to another file by position anywhere in the body (lines 1-16); the only cross-references are within this file (rule 1's territory). No navigational pointer to a separate document either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw/caught" construction anywhere in the body. This is a closer lecture that simulates a hypothetical file, not a recap of a prior module beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict instruction or outcome-reveal pairing anywhere in the body; this file has no demo beat.

chunk 1 carries three self-contained shape descriptions (lines 7-9), each a full claim on its own. chunk 2 carries three bulleted claims (lines 13-15) plus the closer bullet (line 16, "Agents build agents"). Neither chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

chunk 1 header "Three agents using the file" (line 5): body lists exactly three agents (Slack triage / Issue webhook / Scheduled read), each using the file — literally true. chunk 2 header "The file is steady; the agent moves" (line 11): first bullet, line 13, restates the header verbatim ("The file is the steady part; the agent is the moving part") — the header is not contradicted anywhere in the chunk.

Checked all five sub-items against lines 5-16. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction. No anaphora/epistrophe triple (the list at line 14, "Slack thread, issue event, daily schedule…", is an enumeration, not a repeated grammatical frame). No self-grading superlative. No number-plus-retraction. No abstraction-noun stack ("steady part"/"moving part" at lines 11/13 are concrete, not jargon nouns). Verb triplet at line 8 ("it proposes labels, asks for missing info, or splits the issue into smaller tickets") and at line 9 ("which items want to merge, which want to split, which want to die") — each leg answers "what does this concretely mean?" on its own; no empty leg.
